items.name: Add Sheet to Existing Spreadsheet
items.description: Adds a new sheet to a spreadsheet. Supports three sheet types: GRID, OBJECT, and DATA_SOURCE. SHEET TYPES: - GRID (default): Standard spreadsheet with rows/columns. Use properties to set dimensions, tab color, etc. - OBJECT: Sheet containing a chart. Requires objectSheetConfig with chartSpec (basicChart or pieChart). - DATA_SOURCE: Sheet connected to BigQuery. Requires dataSourceConfig with bigQuery spec and bigquery.readonly OAuth scope. OTHER NOTES: - Sheet names must be unique; use forceUnique=true to auto-append suffix (_2, _3) if name exists - For tab colors, use EITHER rgbColor OR themeColor, not both - Avoid 'index' when creating sheets in parallel (causes errors) - OBJECT sheets are created via addChart with position.newSheet=true - DATA_SOURCE sheets require bigquery.readonly OAuth scope Use cases: Add standard grid sheet, create chart on dedicated sheet, connect to BigQuery data source.

items.name: Aggregate Column Data
items.description: Searches for rows where a specific column matches a value and performs mathematical operations on data from another column.

input_parameters.title: AggregateColumnDataRequest

operation.title: Operation
operation.description: The mathematical operation to perform on the target column values.
operation.human_parameter_description: Select the type of calculation you want to perform on the values from the target column.

sheet_name.title: Sheet Name
sheet_name.description: The name of the specific sheet within the spreadsheet. Matching is case-insensitive. If no exact match is found, partial matches will be attempted (e.g., 'overview' will match 'Overview 2025').
sheet_name.human_parameter_description: Specify which sheet in the spreadsheet you want to use for your data aggregation. Matching is case-insensitive and supports partial matches.

search_value.title: Search Value
search_value.description: The exact value to search for in the search column. Case-sensitive by default. If not provided (or if search_column is not provided), all rows in the target column will be aggregated without filtering.
search_value.human_parameter_description: Provide the specific value you want to find in the selected search column. Leave empty to aggregate all rows.

search_column.title: Search Column
search_column.description: The column to search in for filtering rows. Can be a letter (e.g., 'A', 'B') or column name from header row (e.g., 'Region', 'Department'). If not provided, all rows in the target column will be aggregated without filtering.
search_column.human_parameter_description: Indicate the column you want to look through to find matching values. Leave empty to aggregate all rows.

target_column.title: Target Column
target_column.description: The column to aggregate data from. Can be a letter (e.g., 'C', 'D') or column name from header row (e.g., 'Sales', 'Revenue').
target_column.human_parameter_description: This is the column from which you want to gather and perform calculations on data.

case_sensitive.title: Case Sensitive
case_sensitive.description: Whether the search should be case-sensitive.
case_sensitive.human_parameter_description: Decide if the search should match upper and lower case letters exactly.

has_header_row.title: Has Header Row
has_header_row.description: Whether the first row contains column headers. If True, column names can be used for search_column and target_column.
has_header_row.human_parameter_description: Indicate if your data has column names in the first row, which helps in identifying columns by name.

spreadsheet_id.title: Spreadsheet Id
spreadsheet_id.description: The unique identifier of the Google Sheets spreadsheet.
spreadsheet_id.human_parameter_description: The unique ID for locating the specific spreadsheet you want to work with.

percentage_total.title: Percentage Total
percentage_total.description: For percentage operation, the total value to calculate percentage against. If not provided, uses sum of all values in target column.
percentage_total.human_parameter_description: If you're calculating a percentage, this is the total value to compare against. If you leave this blank, it will use the total of the target column.

sheet_id.title: Sheet Id
sheet_id.description: The numeric identifier of the specific sheet (tab) within the spreadsheet. Defaults to 0 (the first sheet) if neither sheet_id nor sheet_name is provided. Use GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SHEET_NAMES or GOOGLESHEETS_FIND_WORKSHEET_BY_TITLE to obtain the sheet_id from a sheet name.

sheet_name.title: Sheet Name
sheet_name.description: The name (title) of the sheet/tab where the column will be added. If provided, the action will look up the sheet_id automatically. If both sheet_id and sheet_name are provided, sheet_id takes precedence.
sheet_name.human_parameter_description: Enter the name of the sheet/tab where you want to add the column. This is an alternative to specifying sheet_id.

insert_index.title: Insert Index
insert_index.description: The 0-based index at which the new column will be inserted. For example, an index of 0 inserts the column before the current first column (A), and an index of 1 inserts it between the current columns A and B.
insert_index.human_parameter_description: Specify the position where the new column should be added, counting from the left.

spreadsheet_id.title: Spreadsheet Id
spreadsheet_id.description: The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet where the column will be created.
spreadsheet_id.human_parameter_description: Provide the unique ID of the Google Spreadsheet where you want to add the new column.

response_ranges.title: Response Ranges
response_ranges.description: Limits the ranges of the spreadsheet to include in the response. Only used if includeSpreadsheetInResponse is true.
response_ranges.human_parameter_description: Limit the response to only include data from specific ranges in the spreadsheet.

inherit_from_before.title: Inherit From Before
inherit_from_before.description: If true, the new column inherits properties (e.g., formatting, width) from the column immediately to its left (the preceding column). If false (default), it inherits from the column immediately to its right (the succeeding column). This is ignored if there is no respective preceding or succeeding column.
inherit_from_before.human_parameter_description: Decide if the new column should copy properties from the column on its left.

response_include_grid_data.title: Response Include Grid Data
response_include_grid_data.description: If true, grid data will be included in the response (only used if includeSpreadsheetInResponse is true).
response_include_grid_data.human_parameter_description: Set to true to include the actual cell data in the response when includeSpreadsheetInResponse is also true.

include_spreadsheet_in_response.title: Include Spreadsheet In Response
include_spreadsheet_in_response.description: If true, the updated spreadsheet will be included in the response. Defaults to true if not specified.
include_spreadsheet_in_response.human_parameter_description: Set to true if you want the full updated spreadsheet data returned in the response.

examples: WITH ActiveUsers AS (SELECT * FROM "Users" WHERE status = 'active') SELECT name, email FROM ActiveUsers

Use table names (sheet names) in FROM/INTO clauses, not A1 range notation. The query must include proper SQL clauses (e.g., SELECT columns FROM table, not just a column name or condition). Example: SELECT * FROM "Sheet1" WHERE A = 'value' (correct) instead of just A = 'value' (incorrect).

items.description: Tool to set or clear data validation rules (including dropdowns) on a range in Google Sheets. Use when you need to apply dropdown lists, range-based dropdowns, or custom formula validation to cells.

input_parameters.title: SetDataValidationRuleRequest

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Operation mode: 'SET' applies a validation rule to the range, 'CLEAR' removes any existing validation from the range.

strict.title: Strict
strict.description: Whether to reject invalid data (true) or show a warning (false). Default is true.

values.title: Values
values.description: List of allowed values for dropdown. Required when validation_type='ONE_OF_LIST'. Each item becomes a dropdown option.

formula.title: Formula
formula.description: Custom formula for validation. Required when validation_type='CUSTOM_FORMULA'. Formula should evaluate to TRUE/FALSE. Example: '=A1>10'.

sheet_id.title: Sheet Id
sheet_id.description: The unique sheet ID (numeric identifier) where the validation rule will be applied. The first sheet created in a spreadsheet typically has ID 0, while additional sheets get unique IDs (e.g., 1534097477). If a sheet is deleted, its ID is never reused - so if the original first sheet (ID 0) was deleted, attempting to use 0 will fail. Always verify the actual sheet ID exists using GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SPREADSHEET_INFO action (check 'sheets[].properties.sheetId' field).

end_row_index.title: End Row Index
end_row_index.description: Ending row index (0-based, exclusive) for the validation range. To apply to row 1 only, use start_row_index=0 and end_row_index=1.

input_message.title: Input Message
input_message.description: Optional message shown to the user when they select the cell. Helpful hint about what values are expected.

show_custom_ui.title: Show Custom Ui
show_custom_ui.description: Whether to show a dropdown UI for list-based validation. Default is true. Set to true for dropdown lists.

spreadsheet_id.title: Spreadsheet Id
spreadsheet_id.description: The unique identifier of the Google Sheets spreadsheet. Can be found in the spreadsheet URL between '/d/' and '/edit'.

source_range_a1.title: Source Range A1

start_row_index.title: Start Row Index
start_row_index.description: Starting row index (0-based, inclusive) for the validation range. Row 1 is index 0.

validation_type.title: Validation Type
validation_type.description: Type of validation rule to apply. Required when mode='SET'. Dropdown types: 'ONE_OF_LIST' (dropdown from list), 'ONE_OF_RANGE' (dropdown from range). Number validations: 'NUMBER_GREATER', 'NUMBER_GREATER_THAN_EQ', 'NUMBER_LESS', 'NUMBER_LESS_THAN_EQ', 'NUMBER_EQ', 'NUMBER_NOT_EQ', 'NUMBER_BETWEEN', 'NUMBER_NOT_BETWEEN'. Text validations: 'TEXT_CONTAINS', 'TEXT_NOT_CONTAINS', 'TEXT_EQ', 'TEXT_NOT_EQ', 'TEXT_IS_EMAIL', 'TEXT_IS_URL' (Note: TEXT_STARTS_WITH and TEXT_ENDS_WITH are only for conditional formatting, not data validation). Date validations: 'DATE_EQ', 'DATE_BEFORE', 'DATE_AFTER', 'DATE_ON_OR_BEFORE', 'DATE_ON_OR_AFTER', 'DATE_BETWEEN', 'DATE_NOT_BETWEEN', 'DATE_NOT_EQ', 'DATE_IS_VALID'. items.name: Upsert Rows (Smart Update/Insert)
items.description: Upsert rows - update existing rows by key, append new ones. Automatically handles column mapping and partial updates. Use for: CRM syncs (match Lead ID), transaction imports (match Transaction ID), inventory updates (match SKU), calendar syncs (match Event ID). Features: - Auto-adds missing columns to sheet - Partial column updates (only update Phone + Status, preserve other columns) - Column order doesn't matter (auto-maps by header name) - Prevents duplicates by matching key column Example inputs: - Contact update: keyColumn='Email', headers=['Email','Phone','Status'], data=[['john@ex.com','555-0101','Active']] - Inventory sync: keyColumn='SKU', headers=['SKU','Stock','Price'], data=[['WIDGET-001',50,9.99],['GADGET-002',30,19.99]] - CRM lead update: keyColumn='Lead ID', headers=['Lead ID','Score','Status'], data=[['L-12345',85,'Hot']] - Partial update: keyColumn='Email', headers=['Email','Phone'] (only updates Phone, preserves Name/Address/etc)

input_parameters.title: UpsertRowsRequest

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: 2D array of data rows to upsert. IMPORTANT: If 'headers' is NOT provided, the FIRST row is treated as column headers and remaining rows as data - so you need at least 2 rows (1 header + 1 data). If 'headers' IS provided separately, then ALL rows in this array are treated as data rows. Each row should have the same number of values as headers. If a row has MORE values than headers: with strict_mode=true (default), an error is returned showing which rows are affected; with strict_mode=false, extra values are silently truncated. If a row has FEWER values than headers, an error is returned during execution. Cell values can be strings, numbers, booleans, or null. Example with headers provided: headers=['Email','Status'], rows=[['john@ex.com','Active']] (1 data row). Example without headers: rows=[['Email','Status'],['john@ex.com','Active']] (row 1 = headers, row 2 = data).
rows.human_parameter_description: Enter the actual data rows you want to insert or update. Ensure each row matches the provided headers.

headers.title: Headers
headers.description: List of column names for the data. These will be matched against sheet headers. If a column doesn't exist in the sheet, it will be added automatically. Order doesn't need to match sheet order. Can be auto-derived from the first row in 'rows' if not provided. Example inputs: ['Email', 'Phone', 'Status'] for contact updates, ['Lead ID', 'Name', 'Score'] for CRM, ['SKU', 'Stock', 'Price'] for inventory.
headers.human_parameter_description: Provide the names of the columns you want to upsert data for. They should match the existing headers in the sheet.

keyColumn.title: Key Column
keyColumn.description: The column NAME (header text) to use as unique identifier for matching rows. Must be an actual header name from the sheet (e.g., 'Email', 'Lead ID', 'SKU'), NOT a column letter (e.g., 'A', 'B', 'C'). If you provide a column letter like 'A', it will be automatically converted to the header name at that column position. If neither 'key_column' nor 'key_column_index' is provided, defaults to the first column (index 0).
keyColumn.human_parameter_description: Specify the name of the column that contains unique identifiers to match existing rows.

sheetName.title: Sheet Name
sheetName.description: The name of the sheet/tab within the spreadsheet. Note: Google Sheets creates default sheets with localized names based on account language (e.g., 'Sheet1' for English, '工作表1' for Chinese, 'Hoja1' for Spanish, 'Feuille1' for French, 'Planilha1' for Portuguese, 'Лист1' for Russian). If you specify a common default name and the sheet is not found, the action will automatically use the first sheet if only one exists.
sheetName.human_parameter_description: Enter the name of the sheet you want to update within the spreadsheet.

strictMode.title: Strict Mode
strictMode.description: Controls how rows with mismatched column counts are handled. When True (default), an error is returned if any row has more values than headers - the error message shows exactly which rows are affected and what values would need to be removed. When False, extra values are silently truncated to match the header count. Set to False only if you explicitly want automatic truncation of extra values.
strictMode.human_parameter_description: When enabled (default), rejects rows with extra values. Disable to auto-truncate extra values.

tableStart.title: Table Start
tableStart.description: Cell where the table starts (where headers are located). Defaults to 'A1'. Use this if your table is offset (e.g., 'C5', 'D10').
tableStart.human_parameter_description: Specify the cell where your data headers start in the sheet, such as 'A1' or 'C5'.

spreadsheetId.title: Spreadsheet Id
spreadsheetId.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Must be a non-empty string, typically a 44-character alphanumeric string found in the spreadsheet URL.
spreadsheetId.human_parameter_description: Provide the unique ID of the Google Spreadsheet where you want to upsert rows.

key_column_index.title: Key Column Index
key_column_index.description: The 0-based column index to use as unique identifier for matching rows. Alternative to 'key_column' - will be converted to column name using headers. If neither 'key_column' nor 'key_column_index' is provided, defaults to 0 (first column). Example: 0 for first column, 1 for second column.

items.description: Returns a range of values from a spreadsheet. Use when you need to read data from specific cells or ranges in a Google Sheet.

range.title: Range
range.description: The A1 notation or R1C1 notation of the range to retrieve values from. If the sheet name contains spaces or special characters, wrap the sheet name in single quotes (e.g., "'My Sheet'!A1:B2"). Without single quotes, the API will return a 400 error for sheet names with spaces. Examples: 'Sheet1!A1:B3', "'Sheet With Spaces'!A1:D5", 'A1:D5' (no sheet name uses first visible sheet), 'Sheet1!A:A' (entire column), 'SheetName' (entire sheet).
range.human_parameter_description: Specify the range of cells you want to retrieve using A1 notation (e.g., 'A1:B10', 'Sheet1!A1:C5'). If the sheet name contains spaces or special characters, enclose the sheet name in single quotes (e.g., "'My Sheet'!A1:B2").

end_row.title: End Row
end_row.description: 1-based row number to stop reading at (inclusive). Use with start_row for pagination to avoid large response errors. Example: start_row=501, end_row=1000 fetches rows 501-1000.
end_row.human_parameter_description: Last row to read (1-based). Leave empty to read to the end of the range.

start_row.title: Start Row
start_row.description: 1-based row number to start reading from (inclusive). Use with end_row for pagination to avoid large response errors. Example: start_row=1, end_row=500 fetches the first 500 rows.
start_row.human_parameter_description: First row to read (1-based). Leave empty to start from the beginning of the range.

spreadsheet_id.title: Spreadsheet Id
spreadsheet_id.description: The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet from which to retrieve values. This is the long alphanumeric string found in the spreadsheet URL between '/d/' and '/edit' (e.g., '1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms'). WARNING: Do NOT use the spreadsheet name or title (e.g., 'My Sales Report'); you must use the actual ID from the URL.
spreadsheet_id.human_parameter_description: Provide the unique ID of the spreadsheet you want to extract values from. The ID is the long alphanumeric string in the URL between '/d/' and '/edit'. Do NOT use the spreadsheet name.

major_dimension.title: MajorDimension
major_dimension.human_parameter_description: Indicate whether you want your data organized by rows or columns. If you're not sure, it defaults to rows.

value_render_option.title: Value Render Option
value_render_option.description: How values should be rendered in the output. FORMATTED_VALUE: Values are calculated and formatted (default). UNFORMATTED_VALUE: Values are calculated but not formatted. FORMULA: Values are not calculated; the formula is returned instead.
value_render_option.human_parameter_description: Choose how you want the values to be displayed. You can get the formatted version, an unformatted version, or just the underlying formula.

date_time_render_option.description: How dates, times, and durations should be represented in the output. SERIAL_NUMBER: Dates are returned as serial numbers (default). FORMATTED_STRING: Dates returned as formatted strings.
date_time_render_option.human_parameter_description: Select how you want dates and times to be shown. You can use serial numbers or get formatted strings.

items.name: Update spreadsheet values
items.description: Tool to set values in a range of a Google Spreadsheet. Use when you need to update or overwrite existing cell values in a specific range.

range.title: Range
range.description: The A1 notation of the range to update values in (e.g., 'Sheet1!A1:C2', 'MySheet!C:C', or 'A1:D5'). Must be actual cell references, not placeholder values. If the sheet name is omitted (e.g., 'A1:B2'), the operation applies to the first visible sheet. IMPORTANT: The range must not exceed the sheet's grid dimensions. By default, new sheets have 1000 rows and 26 columns (A-Z). If you need to write to columns beyond Z (e.g., AA, AB), first expand the sheet using GOOGLESHEETS_APPEND_DIMENSION or check the current dimensions using GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SPREADSHEET_INFO.
range.human_parameter_description: Specify the exact range in the spreadsheet where you want the values to be updated. Use A1 notation for accuracy. Ensure the range does not exceed the sheet's current grid dimensions.

values.title: Values
values.description: The data to write. This is an array of arrays, the outer array representing all the data and each inner array representing a major dimension. Each item in the inner array corresponds with one cell.
values.human_parameter_description: Provide the data you want to write into the specified range. This should be structured in arrays to correspond to the layout of the spreadsheet.

spreadsheet_id.title: Spreadsheet Id
spreadsheet_id.description: The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet to update. This ID can be found in the URL of the spreadsheet (e.g., https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/{spreadsheet_id}/edit). Must be a non-empty string.
spreadsheet_id.human_parameter_description: Provide the unique ID of the spreadsheet you want to update. You can find this ID in the spreadsheet's URL.

major_dimension.title: Major Dimension
major_dimension.description: The major dimension of the values. ROWS (default) means each inner array is a row of values. COLUMNS means each inner array is a column of values. Defaults to ROWS if unspecified.
major_dimension.human_parameter_description: Indicate whether your data is organized by rows or columns. Use ROWS for row-wise data or COLUMNS for column-wise data.

auto_expand_sheet.title: Auto Expand Sheet
auto_expand_sheet.description: If True (default), automatically expands the sheet's dimensions (adds columns/rows) when the target range exceeds the current grid limits. If False, the operation will fail with an error if the range exceeds grid limits.
auto_expand_sheet.human_parameter_description: Enable automatic expansion of the sheet when writing beyond current grid limits. Disable to receive an error instead.

value_input_option.title: Value Input Option
value_input_option.description: How the input data should be interpreted. RAW: Values are stored exactly as entered, without parsing (dates, formulas, etc. remain as strings). USER_ENTERED: Values are parsed as if typed by a user (numbers stay numbers, strings prefixed with '=' become formulas, etc.).
value_input_option.human_parameter_description: Choose how the input values should be treated. Select RAW for exact values or USER_ENTERED for automatic parsing like a user would do.

include_values_in_response.title: Include Values In Response
include_values_in_response.description: Determines if the update response should include the values of the cells that were updated. By default, responses do not include the updated values.
include_values_in_response.human_parameter_description: Decide if you want the updated cell values included in the response after the operation.

response_value_render_option.human_parameter_description: Specify how you would like the values in the response to be displayed. Choose formatted for a user-friendly view or unformatted for raw values.

response_datetime_render_option.human_parameter_description: Indicate how you want dates and times to appear in the response. Choose serial number for numeric representation or formatted string for a more readable format.
